decisions.rationale: The coordinated string 'breast-ovarian cancer' refers to two separate diseases (breast cancer and ovarian cancer) in one contiguous span, so it is a Composite Mention even though it modifies 'families'.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §2 (Composite Mention); §3 (Modifier) considered and rejected because two diseases are denoted

decisions.rationale: 'Breast Cancer Linkage Consortium' is the name of an organization, not a reference to a disease, so it is not annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (only disease mentions are annotated); What NOT to Annotate (non-disease usage)

decisions.rationale: The breast-ovary cancer-family syndrome is described as genetically heterogeneous, meaning it denotes a family of multiple specific diseases rather than one fixed disease definition.
'cancer of the breast and ovaries' is one contiguous string that refers to two separate diseases, breast cancer and ovarian cancer.
'breast-ovary cancer' coordinates breast cancer and ovary cancer as two separate diseases in one contiguous string; the composite rule applies even though the string modifies 'families'.
'breast and ovarian cancer' is one contiguous string referring to two distinct cancers, breast cancer and ovarian cancer.
'breast cancer or ovarian cancer' lists two distinct specific diseases within one contiguous string.
'ovarian cancer' names a single specific disease with no further categorization, and the term 'cancer' is retained by the rules.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease); What NOT to Annotate §4 (cancer and tumor are retained)

decisions.rationale: 'male breast cancer' identifies a distinct form of breast cancer, so the gender term is included as part of the disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate §2 (gender exception for male breast cancer); What to Annotate §1

decisions.rationale: 'male breast cancer' identifies a distinct form of breast cancer, so the gender term is included as part of the disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate §2 (gender exception for male breast cancer); What to Annotate §1

decisions.rationale: 'ovarian cancers' is the plural form referring to the specific disease ovarian cancer, which is a single defined disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease); What NOT to Annotate §4 (cancer retained)

decisions.rationale: The breast-ovarian cancer-family syndrome is stated to be genetically heterogeneous, so it denotes a family of multiple specific diseases rather than one specific disease.
'breast cancer' is a specific disease mention referring to one defined disease.
'ovarian cancer' is a specific disease mention referring to one defined disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease); What NOT to Annotate §4 (cancer retained)
